The knowledge base has no matching document, so I’m searching the public web for the paper and its fish-bag calculation.
```python
web_results = await web_search('"Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragon’s Diet?" fish bag volume', max_results=5)
print(web_results)
```
I’m retrieving the paper or a reliable indexed copy from the search results to verify the exact numerical volume.
```python
paper_web = await web_search('"Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragon\'s Diet" University of Leicester PDF', max_results=10)
print(paper_web)
```
The first search did not expose a result in the returned context, so I’m using a narrower query focused on the paper’s equation and units.
```python
volume_search = await web_search('"fish bag" "Hiccup" volume m^3', max_results=10)
print(volume_search)
```
I’m checking the University of Leicester publication directly by title and will use the paper’s reported value rather than infer it from the fish dimensions.
```python
direct_search = await web_search('University of Leicester "Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish"')
print(direct_search)
```
I’m searching for the article text via the journal title and the distinctive “fish bag” phrase.
```python
article_search = await web_search('"fish bag" "Can Hiccup"')
print(article_search)
```
I’m issuing one final broad search for the exact numerical result, including likely scientific notation.
```python
exact_search = await web_search('"Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragon\'s Diet?" "m3"', max_results=10)
print(exact_search)
```
